key_insight: Oxygen vacancy formation energies across binary main-group metal oxides largely track cation reducibility and can be predicted using crystal reduction potential and band gap.
engineering_relevance: Bulk-property predictions could accelerate oxide screening for solid-oxide fuel cells and solar thermochemical fuel production.
method: Survey 39 oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Use ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed neutral-vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model and retain its two dominant descriptors.
evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: The model is evaluated on neutral vacancies in main-group oxides; its largest residuals flag cases where electron accommodation departs from cation reduction.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
